Do It [02:08] - A short film my friends and I made for a 48hr film festival. Let us know what you think!
Thanks for the feedback. We were aiming for a twist ending so I'm glad you enjoyed it!
I'm glad you enjoyed it, that means a lot to us as storytellers! :)

Very cool!

As a filmmaker myself here are some things I noticed. ( I love to critically review films, these are all merely suggestions that popped into my head that I'd like to share with you. Not a rant! )

Looking at the story, I thought it was a really neat idea and the ending wrapped everything up nicely. That being said, I thought it could have been even stronger if all of the "tasks" that Matt was trying to accomplish were all things that were much more difficult because of his leg injury. I thought the best one of these tasks was Matt trying to summon the courage to call up a girl. An example of one I thought didn't really follow the plot was Matt doing pull-ups, I didn't see how this was supposed to be any more difficult and made it harder for the end of the film to tie everything together.

The editing was pretty good, I especially like the action cut from the pull up bar to the couch. The colors seemed a bit washed out, this could have been an artistic choice, but would have liked to have some color grading that reflected Matt's struggle and then maybe something different for the reveal at the end.

The DP work was really well done and I was really impressed with the shot where Matt's sort of voice in his head is in a mirror, this gave me a feeling that he was somehow disconnected from the immediate setting. The only thing I would have done differently was the reveal, I thought it was really awesome to go into that extreme closeup on Matt to get a very intimate sense of how he was feeling emotionally but instead of dollying back out, I would have done a hard cut to a wide shot of Matt alone in the room shortly after his final line. I feel like that would have been a more intense and impactful reveal

The sound was good, there was some ambient noise in the background but nothing too distracting. I thought the piece could have really benefited from some music.I thought some kind of alarm or something going off in the beginning would have been good as well, kind of foreshadowing that Matt is by himself and that he doesn't rely on the other character. Maybe he hesitates to the alarm going off but this voice in his head forces him to get up and carry on.

Very cool film, I'll keep track of your channel. I can't wait to see what else you can come up with.

Hey, thank you so much for this!! We love getting feedback and reviews to learn on what we can work on.

The tasks were something that we tried to put a lot of thought into, I personally always felt the dishwashing scene was the weakest. The pull-ups for us was to serve the additional function of just not a task but also a bit of character development. In the story it wasn't terribly clear but we did hint at the fact that Matt was a vet (we included army shoes and an army pin in the opening shot) so we figured he'd try to at least get back in shape as part of the road to his recovery. I could see how it doesn't tie together as great as the other tasks though.

Color was something we might play around with a bit more. I don't think we considered using it as part of the reveal, thats a conversation I'll have to have with our DP to see if he has any additional thoughts. Thanks for getting us thinking about it though!

That's a good note on the reveal. I'd like to go back and see if we have the footage to maybe cut something like that together, although I think in terms of the overall style of the film we had agreed on a very active camera. But I do see how a contrast to the style could maybe even strengthen the reveal.

Many thanks for the DP compliments. I will make sure to pass on your kind words and notes to Ben, I'm sure he will really appreciate it!

Sound was probably the hardest part for us. None of us were really sound guys, especially when we made this film, so we really appreciate feedback on the sound design.

Thank you very much for the support though, feel free to share your feedback with us on any of our projects it is very appreciated!

Haha sorry about that, it received a similar reaction at the film festival.

We have some lighter films on our youtube channel but this one was our go at a more dramatic story.
